hook: Pushing on a stuck car until your arms ache changes nothing about the car, yet a gentle shove on a shopping cart sends it rolling. In physics, work means energy moved into or out of an object by a force acting along a displacement, and that definition explains why effort alone does not count.

prereq.why: K = ½mv², with the speed squared.

prereq.q: In a right triangle, the side next to angle θ equals the hypotenuse times
Kinetic friction on a sliding crate points
prereq.why: Kinetic friction opposes the sliding of the surfaces.

figure.caption: Work done by each force on a crate pulled 4.0 m: the rope does positive work, friction negative work, and the normal and gravitational forces none.

chain.cause: A force acts on an object while the object moves
chain.effect: the force does work W = F d cos θ, using only the component along the displacement

chain.cause: The force has a component along the motion
chain.effect: the work is positive and energy enters the object

chain.cause: The force opposes the motion (like kinetic friction)
chain.effect: the work is negative and energy leaves the object

chain.cause: The force is perpendicular to the motion
chain.effect: it does no work and does not change the speed

chain.cause: All the works on an object are added
chain.effect: the net work equals the change in kinetic energy: W_net = ΔK

ideas: Work is energy moved into or out of a system by a force acting along a displacement: W = F d cos θ, with θ between the force and the displacement. It is a scalar, in joules.
Positive work adds energy, negative work removes it, and a force perpendicular to the motion does none.
The work-energy theorem: the net work done on an object equals its change in kinetic energy, W_net = ΔK.
Work by a varying force is the area under its force-position graph.
Kinetic friction does negative work that grows with the path length, even on a round trip.

misconception.wrong: Gravity does work on a crate dragged across a level floor, because gravity acts on it the whole time.
misconception.right: A force does work only through its component along the displacement. Gravity is vertical and the motion is horizontal, so gravity does zero work here.

summary: Work is W = F d cos θ: energy carried into an object (positive) or out of it (negative) by a force along a displacement. Perpendicular forces do none. The net work equals ΔK, and a varying force's work is the area under its force-position graph.
